description.purpose: A web page on a screen, as a cell. One Chromium-based browser per member, a browser context per identity, a page per card, and each page's picture streamed onto a topic of the display's own socket -- so a person looks at the page itself rather than at somebody's summary of it, and can reach into it with a pointer, a finger or a keyboard. The browser is a PREREQUISITE, not a delivery: it comes from the machine's package system, brings its own confinement with it, and this template points at it.
description.use_when: Wherever an application would otherwise have to choose between a link somebody has to click and an iframe a site is allowed to refuse. Instantiate it once per member under the mount a display's page: joins should reach, point chromium_path at the installed browser, and draw four edges in the same mutation: open, close and navigate in, and the page lane back out.
description.not_in_scope: No browser ships with this template, and no cache path, no AppArmor profile and no sandbox switch either: a browser whose own sandbox does not hold does not start, and there is no way to say otherwise. No persistence of a logged-in session -- a context is an identity and an ephemeral one, so a restart is a logged-out browser and that is the design rather than a gap. No video codec: the picture is a JPEG screencast, and a codec is a later wave. No opinion about what to open: the addresses come from the application, and this cell holds pages rather than choosing them.
examples: PORTS - Entry: one tool_call turn per verb -- in_open {page, url, context?, viewport?}, in_navigate {page, url}, in_close {page}, in_context_close {context}. Exit: a receipt per message and a page emission per state change, plus error for a spawn, a CDP or a crash failure.

THE TOPIC IS THE PAGE - a display joins page:<page> on its own socket, the mount table hands the join to this cell, and the frames travel as an image broadcast: sixteen bytes of head (width, height, scroll x, scroll y, big-endian) and then the JPEG. Inputs come back on the same link as text, so a keystroke is never a message.
a page nobody has looked at for five minutes -> its target is closed and its context kept; the next join or navigation opens it again, in the same identity, and nobody had to be told it was gone
